reading.body:
Flexential Fort Lauderdale publishes 3.15 MW of IT capacity across 64,164 square feet of technical space, making it a small facility by AI training standards where individual clusters routinely exceed this by an order of magnitude.

At typical colocation density of 10 kW per rack, this capacity supports roughly 315 racks; at 40 kW per rack typical for AI training, it supports roughly 79 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure represents their claim. The size constrains the workloads this facility can host. Large-scale model training requires centralized power and cooling at scales this site does not offer. Inference workloads and enterprise applications fit more naturally within these bounds.

The certification stack, spanning SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, HIPAA, and SSAE 18, qualifies the facility for regulated compliance hosting in finance, healthcare, and payment processing. This certifications-first posture indicates a colocation environment built for tenant isolation and audit rather than for the consolidated power delivery that AI training demands. The operator has not published tenant information, so the actual workloads present remain unknown.

Within the narrow published pool of Florida facilities this site has measured, this campus contributes 3.15 MW of 7.54 MW on record, or 42 percent. That figure reflects data collection limits across 13 mapped Florida facilities, not comprehensive market coverage. For organizations evaluating South Florida for AI infrastructure, this site offers regulated hosting suited to inference or enterprise workloads, not large-scale model training.
